# Storyboard: How Fast Is Sound?

Type: explainer · Audience: all-ages · Host outfit: lab-coat
Music mood: curious
Total: 22.6 s, 3 scenes, host step-ins: scenes 1, 3; new place: none; custom moves: none; 0 sound effects

## Scene 1: Speed in three materials
- **Place:** `countryside`, variant `day` (library)
- **Duration:** 11.975 s (360 frames)
- **Idea:** Sound is much faster in water and steel than in air.
- **Host:** step-in — stands at `rail-near` in the world
- **Cast:** friend (`extra-1`, casual) at `rail-far`
- **Beats:**
  1. "Sound…" (0) — the host, standing by the rail with a hammer, waves; the title shows; the camera pulls back over the railway. Moves: hold host; gesture host; title "How Fast Is Sound?" on ``; camera pull_out `rail-near` ×0.7
  2. "In…" (6) — the host strikes the rail as the camera moves in; sound rings spread slowly through the air around him. Moves: use host on "air" (7); rings rail-near on "air" (7); label "Air: 343 m/s" on `rail-near` on "343" (11); camera push_in `rail-near` ×1.1
  3. "In…" (15) — the camera moves to the lake; ripples of sound race through the water, faster than in the air. Moves: camera push_in `lake` ×0.95 on "water" (16); rings lake on "water" (16); label "Water: 1,480 m/s" on `lake` on "1,480" (18)
  4. "And…" (19) — back at the rail the host strikes again; a pulse races along the steel to the friend, who jumps in surprise. Moves: camera cut `rail-near` ×1.1; use host on "steel" (21); pulse_along rail on "steel" (21); tag_follow "Steel: ≈6,000 m/s" on `pulse`; camera follow `pulse` ×1.0 on "steel" (21); react friend on "6,000" (23); jump friend on "6,000" (23)
- **Text on screen:** "How Fast Is Sound?", "Air: 343 m/s", "Water: 1,480 m/s", "Steel: ≈6,000 m/s" (13 words in 11.975 s)
- **Scale:** true to scale: the rings, ripples and pulse move at speeds in the true ratio 343 : 1,480 : 5,960
- **Facts:** sound travels about 343 m/s in air; about 1,480 m/s in water; nearly 6,000 m/s (about 5,960 m/s) in steel; the rings, ripples and pulse spread at speeds in the true ratio 343 : 1,480 : 5,960
- **Kit warnings:** none
- **Transition:** fade
- **SFX:** none

## Scene 2: Why solids are faster
- **Place:** `countryside`, variant `day` (library)
- **Duration:** 7.375 s (222 frames)
- **Idea:** Tightly linked particles pass a sound wave on faster.
- **Host:** talks from the left slot
- **Cast:** none
- **Beats:**
  1. "In…" (0) — the host wonders; the camera dives into the air above the farm: gas particles fly far apart. Moves: gesture host; camera dive `sky` × into lattice gas
  2. "In…" (8) — back out over the railway, the camera dives into the steel rail: its particles are packed and linked, jiggling together. Moves: camera cut `rail-near` ×1.2; point host; camera dive `rail-near` × on "a" (9) into lattice solid
- **Text on screen:** none
- **Scale:** no sizes, speeds or ratios shown
- **Facts:** gas particles are far apart; solid particles are tightly linked (bonded)
- **Kit warnings:** none
- **Transition:** fade
